issue_snapshot.title: Follow-ups from #8: 2 from the review
issue_snapshot.body:
What the review and QA of PR #28 (for #8) found and did not fix there — filed as it merged, one ticket for the lot.

## From the review

Non-blocking findings the reviewer approved despite: a statement about severity, not a judgement that they are wrong.

### Split-input before/after rows render with the wrong unit ('N shares') whenever the edit did not also change the split type: expenseChanges carries only changed fields, so half.splitType is undefined and inputValueText falls through to `${value} shares`. A percentage 60/40-to-70/30 edit renders 'Ada 6000 shares -> Ada 7000 shares' instead of 'Ada 60% -> Ada 70%', and an exact-split edit shows raw minor units as shares.

> Split-input before/after rows render with the wrong unit ('N shares') whenever the edit did not also change the split type: expenseChanges carries only changed fields, so half.splitType is undefined and inputValueText falls through to `${value} shares`. A percentage 60/40-to-70/30 edit renders 'Ada 6000 shares -> Ada 7000 shares' instead of 'Ada 60% -> Ada 70%', and an exact-split edit shows raw minor units as shares.
> 
> `components/activity-feed.tsx:340`
> 
> Evidence: lib/expenses/validation.ts:220-239 expenseChanges copies only fields whose JSON differs; the PR's own new test in lib/expenses/actions.test.ts ('names the split inputs it carries') pins a percentage-edit payload of exactly {before:{inputs},after:{inputs}} with no splitType; components/activity-feed.tsx:340 passes half.splitType (undefined there) into inputValueText (:346-355) whose last branch returns `${value} shares` instead of formatMinorUnits/formatBasisPoints. Seed fixtures include exact and percentage expenses (lib/seed/fixtures.ts:449,463), so the qa_script step 'edit a seeded expense's description and one split input' reproduces this.
> 
> Fix: Carry the unit context with the inputs: in expenseChanges also copy splitType into both halves when inputs changed and teach EditDetail to render only fields whose before/after values differ, or add the expense's splitType to ActivityRow and prefer it in snapshotValue when half.splitType is undefined.

### seedThroughApp treats a wedged app (10s timeout) the same as no app: AbortSignal.timeout throws inside the try, the catch-all returns null, and runSeed takes the direct path, seeding a private in-process database while reporting success — while the comment directly above states a timeout 'is a reason to stop rather than to take the other path'.

> seedThroughApp treats a wedged app (10s timeout) the same as no app: AbortSignal.timeout throws inside the try, the catch-all returns null, and runSeed takes the direct path, seeding a private in-process database while reporting success — while the comment directly above states a timeout 'is a reason to stop rather than to take the other path'.
> 
> `scripts/seed.ts:126`
> 
> Evidence: scripts/seed.ts:117-129 — fetch with signal AbortSignal.timeout(SEED_TIMEOUT_MS) inside try, catch { return null }; runSeed (:143-157) falls back to direct loadFixtures on null and report() prints 'no app answered ... wrote the fixtures itself'. A timed-out serving app therefore yields exit 0 with fixtures invisible to any browser.
> 
> Fix: Only return null for connection-refused (fetch TypeError); let timeout/abort errors throw so runSeed fails loudly instead of seeding a database no browser reads.

---
